account:
It is day 1 at six in the morning, and I have just woken at home. I have not yet seen today's activity. I should read my appointment book this morning; the schedule I previously read puts office business at eight, a mill grain inspection at ten, lunch at home at noon, council letters at one, tea with my neighbour at three, office again at half past four, and home at seven.

I still have a feeling I may be missing something in town, but nothing I learned yesterday establishes an unusual gathering or secret business. Townsfolk 28 reported seeing the innkeeper carrying a sack of bread at market. I also saw the innkeeper at town hall carrying bread, but my question about guests was heard by the secretary rather than answered by the innkeeper. Bread could simply be supplies for the inn. I visited the inn yesterday evening and found nobody in the rooms I checked, so I did not obtain a firsthand explanation.

My neighbour knew of no visitors or gatherings. They reported that the baker had explained there was no celebration or decoration, and that a glow might have been his oven. That is a secondhand explanation, not something I verified myself. The secretary said no correspondence or new office business had arrived and no news of public importance could be verified. The filed office record confirmed that no accounts, expenses, or payments had been submitted for approval.

For now, ordinary baking and inn provisioning seem plausible explanations; I do not know of any other purpose. I should keep today's appointments, speak directly with people when there is an opportunity, and distinguish what I actually observe from rumours.
